chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim Abū al-ʿAynāʾ al-Hāshimī, a freed slave of ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī by manumission, narrated to me, saying:

I used to enter upon Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), and I would become thirsty while I was with him, but I regarded him with too much reverence to ask for water, so he would say: “O servant, give him water to drink.”
And sometimes I would speak within myself about rising to leave and think about that, so he would say: “O servant, his mount.”

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, the kunyah of Imam al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام)
key_terms.أُجِلُّهُ: I hold him in great reverence

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام) show knowledge of a person’s unspoken thoughts?
ai.summary: This narration describes the refined awareness of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), as he would know the visitor’s unspoken needs and intentions. It highlights his noble character, attentiveness to others, and a sign of his divinely granted knowledge.
